finishes.note: 5–25 µm. Corrosion protection and paint key. Electrically insulating: mask bond points.

finishes.spec: BS EN 2536 / DEF STAN 03-26 / MIL-A-8625 Type III
finishes.note: 25–75 µm for wear. Roughly half grows outward: state whether dims apply before or after.

finishes.name: Chromate conversion
finishes.note: Negligible thickness and electrically conductive: the choice for earth/EMC bonding faces.

finishes.name: Shot peen

finishes.name: Bead blast

specs.callout:
MATERIAL: EN AW-6082-T6 EXTRUDED BAR TO BS EN 755-2
          TOLERANCES TO BS EN 755-3
FINISH:   SULPHURIC ANODISE TO BS EN ISO 7599, 15 µm, NATURAL
          MASK ALL TAPPED HOLES AND FACE 'A' (BOND FACE, CHROMATE ONLY)
NOTE:     DIMENSIONS APPLY AFTER TREATMENT
tips: 6082 is the UK's stocked general-purpose grade: 6061 is the US equivalent and often interchangeable, but confirm before substituting.
Specify T651 rather than T6 for plate you'll machine heavily; the stress relief saves you distortion arguments later.
Extruded properties vary with section thickness: read the right row of EN 755-2, don't quote a single UTS.

specs.name: Aluminium 7075

forms.standard: BS EN 485-2 + BS EN 485-3/-4 (or AMS 4045 / AMS 4078 on aero work)
forms.note: The usual form for machined fittings.
Bare 7075 pits badly: clad or protect.

tempers.note: Peak strength. Susceptible to stress-corrosion cracking in the short-transverse direction.
Overaged. ~10% strength sacrificed for a large gain in SCC resistance: the default for sustained-load fittings.
Intermediate: better exfoliation resistance than T6, more strength than T73.
Annealed for forming, then re-heat-treat.

finishes.name: Chromate conversion
finishes.note: Standard protection before primer; conductive.

finishes.name: Sulphuric anodise
finishes.note: Good corrosion protection; reduces fatigue life slightly: check with stress.

finishes.name: Primer + topcoat
finishes.note: Usually epoxy primer over conversion coating.

finishes.name: Shot peen
finishes.note: Common on fatigue-critical 7075 fittings.

specs.callout:
MATERIAL: EN AW-7075-T7351 PLATE TO BS EN 485-2
FINISH:   CHROMATE CONVERSION TO DEF STAN 03-18 (CLASS B, CONDUCTIVE)
          THEN EPOXY PRIMER TO [PROGRAMME SPEC]
NOTE:     T73 TEMPER MANDATORY. DO NOT SUBSTITUTE T6
          GRAIN DIRECTION AS SHOWN. SHORT-TRANSVERSE LOADING NOT PERMITTED.
tips: If the part sees sustained tensile load in the short-transverse direction, T73 is not optional: this is the classic 7075 failure mode.
7075 is effectively non-weldable. If someone asks to weld it, the answer is a different alloy (7020 or 6082), not a different procedure.
State grain direction on the drawing for anything cut from thick plate.

specs.name: Aluminium 2024

forms.note: The standard airframe skin form.
Needs full protective treatment.

tempers.note: Solution treated, cold worked, naturally aged. The classic sheet temper.
T3 with stress relief by stretching, for plate.
Solution treated and naturally aged.
Artificially aged variants; higher strength, lower toughness.
Annealed for forming; must be re-solution treated afterwards.

finishes.name: Chromate conversion
finishes.note: Standard under primer.

finishes.name: Chromic or sulphuric anodise
finishes.note: Common on airframe detail parts.

finishes.name: Primer
finishes.note: 2024 is not left bare in service.

specs.callout:
MATERIAL: EN AW-2024-T3 ALCLAD SHEET TO BS EN 485-2, 1.6 THK
FINISH:   CHROMATE CONVERSION TO DEF STAN 03-18 + EPOXY PRIMER
NOTE:     DO NOT REMOVE CLADDING BY MACHINING OR ABRASION
          EDGES ISO 13715 -0.1/-0.5, NO BURRS
tips: Never machine or sand through the cladding: you've just removed the corrosion protection the sheet was bought for.
2024 has excellent fatigue behaviour, which is why it survives on airframes; don't swap it for 7075 to gain static strength without checking fatigue.
Effectively non-weldable: use mechanical fastening or bonding.

specs.name: Aluminium 2219

forms.note: The tankage and pressure-shell form.

tempers.note: Solution treated, cold worked, artificially aged. The standard high-strength weldable condition.
Solution treated and aged.
Solution treated and artificially aged (post-weld re-heat-treat route).
Annealed for forming.

finishes.note: Used for weight reduction on tank walls; state the etch allowance.

specs.callout:
MATERIAL: EN AW-2219-T87 PLATE TO AMS 4095
WELD:     PER [WPS] TO BS EN ISO 15614-2. QUALITY LEVEL B TO BS EN ISO 10042
NDT:      100% RT OF WELDS TO BS EN ISO 17636. PT TO BS EN ISO 3452 LEVEL 3
NOTE:     PROOF TEST PER [TEST SPEC]. DIMENSIONS APPLY AT 20 °C.
tips: 2219 is the go-to when you need a weldable aluminium that also works cryogenically: it keeps toughness where 6082 and 7075 can't go.
Weld strength is well below parent strength; design the joint, don't assume parent properties across it.
Consider post-weld re-solution and age (to T62) where the design can take the distortion.

specs.name: Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5)
specs.composition: AMS 4911 (sheet/plate) · AMS 4928 (bar/billet) · ASTM B348 (bar) · ASTM B265 (sheet)

forms.note: The main machining stock. State the annealing condition.
For Ti-6Al-4V tube specifically, confirm the form spec: much Ti tubing is Grade 9.
Grain flow matters: consider a macro-etch requirement.
Also the standard filler wire form.
State powder spec and reuse limits on the drawing.

tempers.note: The common supply condition: good balance of properties.
Higher strength, lower ductility and toughness.
Improved fracture toughness and crack growth; lower ductility.
After machining or welding to control distortion.

finishes.name: Anodise (Type II)
finishes.note: Wear and galling resistance; also colour-codes fasteners.

finishes.name: Chemical film / passivation
finishes.note: Cleaning and passivation after machining.

finishes.name: Shot peen
finishes.note: Fatigue improvement; specify intensity and coverage.

finishes.name: Chemical mill / etch
finishes.note: Also removes the alpha case after hot work. See tips.

finishes.name: Dry film lubricant
finishes.note: Anti-galling on threads and sliding faces.

specs.callout:
MATERIAL: Ti-6Al-4V BAR TO AMS 4928, MILL ANNEALED
NDT:      PT TO BS EN ISO 3452, SENSITIVITY LEVEL 3
NOTE:     ALPHA CASE TO BE REMOVED FROM ALL SURFACES AFTER HOT FORMING
          ANTI-SEIZE ON ALL THREADS PER [SPEC] (TITANIUM GALLS)
          DIMENSIONS APPLY AFTER TREATMENT
tips: Titanium galls against itself and against stainless. Never run Ti on Ti unlubricated: specify anti-seize or a dry film lubricant on threads and sliding faces.
Alpha case (a hard, brittle oxygen-enriched surface layer) forms during hot working. It must be removed by chemical milling or machining, and the drawing should say so.
Machining is slow: low surface speed, high feed, rigid setup, flood coolant, sharp tools. Budget the cycle time realistically.
Fire risk with fine swarf: check your shop's procedures before specifying operations that generate it.

specs.name: Stainless 316L
specs.composition: BS EN 10088-1 (grades) · BS EN 10088-2 (sheet/plate) · BS EN 10088-3 (bar)

forms.note: The standard machining bar form.
Square EN 10059, flat EN 10058, hex EN 10061.
Surface finish designations (1D, 2B, 2R...) are in EN 10088-2.
Use for pressure-retaining systems.
Structural and general engineering.

tempers.note: Solution annealed: the standard supply condition.
Cold drawn / cold drawn and ground: higher strength, lower ductility.
Strength rises with cold work; magnetic permeability can rise too, which matters for some applications.

finishes.name: Passivation
finishes.note: Removes free iron after machining. Do this: machined stainless is not passive.

finishes.name: Electropolish
finishes.note: Improves cleanability and corrosion resistance; slightly reduces dimensions.

finishes.name: Pickling
finishes.note: After welding, to restore the passive layer and remove heat tint.

finishes.name: Bead blast
finishes.note: Cosmetic matt; passivate afterwards.

finishes.name: Mill finishes
finishes.note: Specify the finish designation rather than describing it in words.

specs.callout:
MATERIAL: X2CrNiMo17-12-2 (1.4404) BRIGHT BAR TO BS EN 10088-3
          DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES TO BS EN 10278, h9
FINISH:   PASSIVATE TO BS EN ISO 16048 AFTER MACHINING
NOTE:     NO CARBON STEEL TOOLING OR MEDIA TO CONTACT PART
          EDGES ISO 13715 -0.1/-0.5, NO BURRS
tips: Machined stainless is not corrosion resistant until it is passivated: free iron smeared from tooling will rust. Put passivation on the drawing.
316L work-hardens rapidly: rigid setup, sharp tools, positive feed, never dwell. A rubbing tool makes the next cut worse.
Keep stainless away from carbon steel tooling, brushes and blast media: cross-contamination causes rust spots that look like material defects.
For pressure systems use the EN 10216/10217 tube standards, not the mechanical ones: the acceptance requirements differ.

specs.name: 17-4PH stainless

forms.note: The main form. State condition (A, H900, H1025...).
15-5PH is often preferred for forgings: cleaner, better transverse toughness.
The cast equivalent.

Aged at 480 °C. Highest strength (~1310 MPa), lowest toughness, most SCC-susceptible.
Aged at 550 °C. The common compromise: ~1070 MPa with much better toughness.
Progressively lower strength, higher toughness and better stress-corrosion behaviour.

finishes.name: Nitriding
finishes.note: Where surface hardness is needed; check the effect on the aged condition.

finishes.name: Dry film lubricant
finishes.note: Anti-galling on threads.

specs.callout:
MATERIAL: 17-4PH BAR TO AMS 5643, SUPPLIED CONDITION A
HEAT TREAT: AGE TO CONDITION H1025 PER AMS 2759/3
            FURNACE PYROMETRY TO AMS 2750
FINISH:   PASSIVATE TO BS EN ISO 16048
NOTE:     HARDNESS 35-40 HRC. DIMENSIONS APPLY AFTER HEAT TREATMENT.
tips: The condition is not optional detail: it IS the specification. '17-4PH' alone tells the shop nothing about strength.
Ageing causes a small, predictable dimensional change. Machine in condition A, age, then finish-machine critical features.
H900 is tempting for strength but is the worst condition for stress-corrosion cracking. H1025 or H1075 is usually the right engineering answer.
Prefer 15-5PH for forgings and thick sections: less delta ferrite means better transverse properties.

specs.name: Inconel 718
specs.composition: AMS 5662/5663 (bar) · AMS 5596/5597 (sheet) · BS EN 10302 · ASTM B637

The standard strength condition (AMS 5662/5663).
Higher strength from a worked structure; check availability.

finishes.name: Dry film lubricant

specs.callout:
MATERIAL: INCONEL 718 BAR TO AMS 5662 (SOLUTION TREATED AND AGED)
NDT:      PT TO BS EN ISO 3452 LEVEL 3; UT TO AMS-STD-2154 CLASS A
NOTE:     ANTI-SEIZE ON ALL THREADS PER [SPEC]
          MACHINE WITH RIGID SETUP. SEE PROCESS SHEET
          DIMENSIONS APPLY AFTER HEAT TREATMENT
tips: 718 is one of the hardest common alloys to machine: low surface speed, heavy positive feed, rigid setup, sharp carbide, and never let the tool rub (it work-hardens instantly).
Budget the cycle time honestly. A part that takes 45 minutes in 17-4PH can take several hours in 718, and that dominates the cost, not the £/kg.
Weld in the solution annealed condition, then heat treat. Welding aged material risks cracking.
Above approximately 700 °C the strength decreases quickly. For higher temperatures, use 625, Waspaloy or Haynes.

specs.name: 15CDV6

forms.note: The main machining form.

MATERIAL: 15CDV6 BAR TO AIR 9160C, QUENCHED AND TEMPERED
          UTS 980 MPa MIN
WELD:     PER [WPS] TO BS EN ISO 15614-1. NO POST-WELD HEAT TREATMENT REQUIRED

NOTE:     BAKE FOR HYDROGEN EMBRITTLEMENT RELIEF WITHIN 4 HRS OF PLATING
          PER BS EN ISO 4042 (200 °C, 8 HRS MIN)
tips: The whole reason 15CDV6 exists is that it welds at full strength without post-weld heat treatment. If your design doesn't exploit that, a cheaper steel may do.
Still a high-strength steel: the hydrogen embrittlement bake after plating is mandatory, not advisory. Put the time limit and temperature on the drawing.
No direct BS EN equivalent exists; procure to AIR 9160C and expect a French or German supply chain.

specs.name: 4130 chrome-moly

forms.note: Square EN 10059, flat EN 10058, hex EN 10061.
The classic space-frame and rig tube.

tempers.note: Common supply condition for tube and welded structures.

After welding: worthwhile on any welded frame.

It rusts fast. Specify a finish even for internal test hardware, or it will be brown before the programme finishes.

Oxidation occurs quickly. If a surface is important electrically, plate it or specify handling and storage.

specs.name: Aluminium 7010
specs.composition: BS EN 573-3 · BS EN 515 · AMS 4205 (T7451 plate)

Same short-transverse caution as all 7xxx alloys.

Pistons, impellers, rotating parts.

tempers.note: Solution treated and artificially aged; stretched for bar.
Solution treated, cold worked, aged.
Modified age for improved stability at temperature.

finishes.name: Hard anodise
finishes.note: Where wear resistance is needed at temperature.

tempers.note: Standard supply condition; T651 stress relieved for plate.

Annealed.

finishes.note: Anodises to a cleaner finish than 6082.

specs.name: Stainless 321

specs.name: Stainless 15-5PH

Cleaner than 17-4 in heavy sections.

~1070 MPa. The usual engineering compromise.
Progressively tougher and more SCC resistant.

Higher strength.
